title: fix: share onboarding sessions across admins
body:
## Summary

- Share the site-scoped Setup Assistant onboarding session when it is created or reused so another admin can open the persisted chat instead of hitting `GET /sessions/{id}` 403.
- Bound AI-powered SVG logo generation to one short attempt and rely on the existing deterministic wordmark fallback when the AI call fails or times out.
- Add regression coverage for reused onboarding sessions being shared for a second admin.

## Why

Real browser testing on a LiteSpeed/cPanel WordPress install exposed two standard-hosting failures:

1. `/onboarding/start` returns a site-scoped persisted session ID, but normal session permissions are owner-scoped. A second admin received `403` when the frontend fetched the reused Setup Assistant session.
2. `sd-ai-agent/generate-logo-svg` could spend too much of the background request budget on AI retries. The deterministic fallback is safer than letting logo generation kill or stall the broader setup run.

## Verification

- `php -l includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php`
- `php -l includes/Abilities/GenerateLogoSvgAbility.php`
- `php -l tests/SdAiAgent/Core/OnboardingManagerTest.php`

  - Result: could not run in this local worktree because `phpunit` / `vendor/bin/phpunit` is unavailable.
- Live browser verification on the affected standard-hosting site:
  - temporary second admin could fetch the shared setup session after the fix (`GET /sessions/1` returned 200 instead of 403).

title: fix: propagate Superdav request timeout
body:
## Summary
- Propagates WordPress AI Client SDK request options into Superdav chat-completion requests so the AgentLoop 300s timeout reaches the HTTP transport.
- Adds regression coverage proving Superdav text-generation requests retain PromptBuilder-bound timeout options.
- Updates the WordPress 7 runtime stubs so PHPStan knows about the AI Client request-options surface used at runtime.

## Root cause
`RequestTimeoutFilter` correctly raised `wp_ai_client_default_request_timeout` to `AgentLoop::LOOP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, but `SuperdavAiTextGenerationModel::createRequest()` did not attach `$this->getRequestOptions()` to the SDK `Request`. The SDK transport therefore fell back to WordPress HTTP's short default timeout, causing long setup prompts to fail with repeated 5s network timeouts.

Resolves #2121

## Verification
- Local repro before fix: AgentLoop failed after 5s with `cURL error 28`.
- Local repro after fix: same AgentLoop request succeeded in 14.6s.

title: fix: guard knowledge count db queries
body:
## Summary

- Block the raw `sd-ai-agent/db-query` anti-pattern that joins knowledge sources and chunks directly to collections by `collection_id` for count summaries.
- Return a targeted error with a safer query shape that uses `collections.chunk_count` plus a separate source count.
- Add db-query prompt guardrails so future diagnostic turns avoid the sources × chunks join shape before execution.

## Investigation notes

For superdav42/tgc.church#199.

- The production knowledge tables already have the relevant indexes: unique `collections.slug`, `sources.idx_collection(collection_id)`, and `chunks.idx_collection(collection_id)`.
- The slow query is still expensive because the join shape multiplies each matched collection's source rows by its chunk rows before `GROUP BY`. Read-only `EXPLAIN` showed the direct join walking roughly thousands of source rows and tens of thousands of chunk rows per collection.
- The optimized shape avoids the chunk-table join for this summary: use `sd_ai_agent_knowledge_collections.chunk_count` for chunk totals and a correlated/grouped source count for source totals.
- I did not find this exact SQL hardcoded in the REST collection/stat endpoints; this looks like a raw diagnostic/db-query shape, so the fix protects the db-query ability and the prompt that teaches models to use it.

title: fix: preserve job activity on chat errors
body:
## Summary

- Preserve live job activity when a chat job ends in `error`.
- Reload the persisted session on terminal job errors before showing the error message.
- If the session cannot be reloaded, snapshot the last live tool/thinking activity into a visible assistant message before clearing `liveToolCalls`.
- Apply the same preservation path to the “lost connection while waiting for the job” poll-failure path.

## Reproduction

The reported failing chat had live tool calls in the UI, then showed only:

> Error: Lost connection to the server while waiting for the job to finish. Reload the page to see if anything was saved.

Local DB evidence showed the active job was stuck in `awaiting_client_tools` with pending `sd-ai-agent-js/capture-screenshot` after the content save:

```text
wp_9_sd_ai_agent_active_jobs.id=5
status=awaiting_client_tools
pending_tools=[{"name":"sd-ai-agent-js/capture-screenshot","args":{"fullPage":true}}]
```

Frontend cause: `jobSlice.pollJob()` rendered tool/thinking progress from `liveToolCalls` while the job was running, but terminal error and max-consecutive-poll-failure paths cleared `liveToolCalls` without first reloading or snapshotting the job activity into `currentSessionMessages`.

## Verification

- `npm run lint:js -- src/store/slices/jobSlice.js src/store/__tests__/index.test.js`
- `npm run test:js -- src/store/__tests__/index.test.js --runInBand`
- `npm run build` completed with existing webpack asset-size warnings.

## Notes

- This does not hide the error. The error still appears, but the attempted work remains visible above it so the user can say “try again” with context.

title: Fix #2320: Upgrade customer runtime schema globally
body:
## Summary

- run the idempotent database installer from the global customer-runtime handler at early `init`
- upgrade stale schemas before frontend, REST, WP-CLI, or cron runtime use instead of waiting for an admin request
- add a real-database regression test that removes the runtime tables at DB version `19.5.6` and verifies the global guard recreates them

## Root cause

The runtime tables introduced at DB version `19.6.0` were installed on plugin activation and `admin_init` only. An already-active installation could therefore execute frontend, REST, CLI, or cron runtime paths indefinitely without creating those tables.

`Database::install()` already uses an option-backed version guard, so the new global call is a cheap no-op when the schema is current.

## Verification

- `vendor/bin/phpunit --no-coverage tests/SdAiAgent/Core/DatabaseSchemaTest.php` — 31 tests, 245 assertions
- `composer phpcs` — 8/8 passed

title: Show credit usage by chat session
body:
## Summary

- replace request-level credit ledger noise with usage grouped by owned chat session
- show the model, exact managed-service USD charge, total/input/cached/output tokens, agent loops, and local tool-call count
- provide expandable per-model details and a “Review full session” action
- add `#/chat/{sessionId}` deep links that open the selected conversation in the chat interface
- send only the numeric local session ID to the managed service for billing attribution
- strictly allowlist service session summaries and re-check local WordPress session ownership before exposing titles or review links
- retain purchases, promotions, coupon redemptions, adjustments, and reversals under “Other credit activity”

## Service dependency

body:
## Summary

title: Enforce rendered page quality with preview-first repairs
body:
## Summary

- enforce mutation-bound rendered-page completion gates for Setup and General agents
- validate responsive composition, accessibility, media quality, placeholders, branding, CTA placement, and screenshot-based first impressions
- stage supported repairs to one existing published page in the current user's WordPress autosave instead of mutating the live page
- resolve authenticated preview URLs in the browser through WordPress core's autosaves REST endpoint without persisting preview nonces
- publish only after the exact preview report passes, then run one canonical anonymous smoke test
- reject stale parents, unrelated editor autosaves, unsupported preview fields, second-page scope expansion, and writes when browser preview validation is unavailable
- preserve revision-safe semantic block edits and provider-default protections

## Preview-first scope

The preview workspace intentionally covers one existing published page per run and fields WordPress can faithfully preview: title, content, excerpt, featured media, and block content. New-page publication and theme/global-style/navigation/template changes remain on their existing workflows rather than being represented as atomic page previews.

## Dogfood evidence

Validated against the local WordPress 7.0.2 homepage:

- the staged marker existed only in autosave revision `64`
- the anonymous canonical homepage continued to render the original “Plan your session” copy
- the authenticated core preview rendered the staged marker with `home` semantics, one H1, and one main landmark
- the preview descriptor contained only the core REST path and no preview nonce
- discarding the workspace removed the autosave and left the published page unchanged

title: Show nested abilities and make client-tool retries idempotent
body:
Follow-up to #2470.

## Summary
- resolve the target nested inside `sd-ai-agent/ability-call` for live and persisted progress updates
- show the target's friendly action and canonical ability ID instead of the generic dispatcher
- apply the same target resolution to detailed tool cards, wrapped design-preview results, and nested failures
- make `/chat/tool-result` retries idempotent when an earlier result was accepted and the loop has already reached a newer browser-tool pause
- scope Git-tracked relative paths to their owning plugin or theme, migrate the legacy global `file_path` key, and prevent expected insert races from corrupting REST JSON
- preserve direct tool calls and incomplete dispatcher calls for backward compatibility

## Root-cause evidence
- the original client-tool POST completed and advanced the paused loop, but a duplicate Git-tracking key printed SQL diagnostics before the REST JSON
- the browser therefore retried the already-consumed result against the newer pending call and received `sd_ai_agent_invalid_client_tool_results`
- the new package-scoped key removes the response corruption, while processed-batch recognition safely acknowledges stale delivery retries without replaying results or consuming the newer pause

## Testing
- `pnpm run verify`
- live database migration verified `package_file (package_slug, file_path)` replaced the legacy global `file_path` unique key
- live retry replay returned HTTP 202 with `results_accepted: true` while preserving the newer pending client call

title: Fix Superdav image option compatibility
body:
## Summary

- normalize generic image-generation hints for the bundled `superdav-image` model
- drop unsupported GPT Image `style` and response-format values
- translate legacy `hd` quality and DALL-E landscape/portrait dimensions to GPT Image equivalents

## Root cause and live verification

The chat agent correctly selected the first-party `sd-ai-agent-cloud` provider and `superdav-image` model, but supplied the ability's documented DALL-E-style defaults (`style: natural`, `quality: standard`). The managed alias currently targets `gpt-image-1`, which rejected those values and surfaced a 502.

Before this change, the full agent loop reproduced the 502 twice. With this change, the same agent-loop flow used `superdav-chat-pro` for tool orchestration, called `sd-ai-agent/generate-image`, routed image generation through `superdav-image`, and created WordPress media attachment 24.

The managed-service boundary is also hardened in https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-service/pull/93.

title: feat: add privacy-safe customer conversation review
body:
Resolves #2545

## Summary

- adds an admin-only Customer Conversations list and sanitized transcript detail view
- uses a dedicated normalized review projection rather than exposing runtime rows or normal user sessions
- keeps anonymous public-chat retention disabled by default and requires an explicit widget recording choice before durable storage
- projects already-durable customer-runtime history into the review model, as required for safe upgrade visibility
- provides bounded pagination, expiry cleanup, source-scoped deletion, explicit purge confirmation, and server-side redaction
- preserves customer-runtime execution, idempotency, authorization, and seven-day operational retention contracts

## Architecture decision

The implementation uses a dedicated normalized review projection. Customer and assistant display text is sanitized before projection persistence; private runtime payloads, signed tokens, source hashes, profile snapshots, tool payloads, and internal identifiers are not exposed by review DTOs. Projection writes fail open so review storage cannot block customer responses.

Anonymous widget recording is a separate opt-in setting and remains disabled on install and upgrade. Existing durable customer-runtime records are reconciled in bounded batches because #2545 explicitly requires safely classifiable retained runtime conversations to become reviewable.

## Repair notes

The recovered worker branch initially leaked nested transaction boundaries into WordPress PHPUnit isolation. Commit `a9372a66` changes repository transactions to use savepoints when a caller already owns the transaction. It also rejects writes after expiry, serializes runtime-source deletion against append operations, removes an unused denormalized transcript column, and adds regression coverage.

title: Fix automatic recovery for large provider retries
body:
## Summary

- automatically retry one large provider-retry exhaustion with deterministic compact history
- retain the full conversation and original paused checkpoint when compact recovery fails

A fresh Setup Assistant run completed 39 tool steps, including page, menu, template-part, and default-content mutations, then failed while requesting its final response. - The original paused state is preserved for terminal failures and cleared only after successful recovery.

- acknowledge duplicate result POSTs while the original resume is still running instead of misclassifying them as expired approvals

## Summary

- Replace browser-primary speech with authenticated, capability-driven transcription and synthesis through the private `sd-ai-agent/v1/speech/*` gateway.
- Add bounded `MediaRecorder` capture, strict mono PCM WAV normalization, managed audio chunking/playback, cancellation, object URL cleanup, and explicit opt-in browser fallback.
- Add a shared turn coordinator for push-to-talk and voice mode across the main chat and floating widget, including response identity tracking, barge-in, session/page cleanup, and deterministic playback ownership.
- Scope speech preferences to the current WordPress user, expose managed voice/speed settings, preserve accessible status behavior, and document the interaction contract in `DESIGN.md`.
- Add focused recorder, speech utility, synthesis, coordinator, and managed Playwright coverage while keeping the widget panel within its entry budget.

## Security and lifecycle

- Browser clients never receive the site-scoped Superdav credential.
- Audio and text use authenticated private REST routes; captured audio is retained only for one transcription request, while accepted transcripts follow the normal chat-message lifecycle.
- Recording, transcription, synthesis, playback, media tracks, requests, and object URLs are stopped or released on cancellation, failure, session changes, page hiding, and unmount.
- Microphone capture starts only from a fresh user gesture and never restarts automatically after playback.
- Browser-native synthesis fallback remains disabled unless the current user explicitly enables it.

title: fix: preserve idless Gemini tool cycles
body:
## Summary

- Preserve an empty internal ID when a provider returns an idless function call instead of replacing it with `unknown`.
- Keep the resulting function response paired with its call during conversation-history validation.
- Add focused coverage for the resolver-to-`ConversationTrimmer` path.

## Why

Gemini 2.5 can return function calls without IDs. The resolver previously assigned the response ID `unknown`, while the original call normalized to an empty ID. `ConversationTrimmer::validate_tool_pairs()` treated that completed cycle as mismatched and removed both messages before the next provider request, causing the model to repeat the same tool call until the loop limit.

The companion Google provider change in WordPress/ai-provider-for-google#45 preserves real Gemini 3 IDs and omits this empty compatibility sentinel from older-model request payloads.

## Files

- `includes/Core/AbilityFunctionResolver.php`: retain an empty internal ID for idless provider calls.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/AbilityFunctionResolverTest.php`: prove the response stays paired through history validation.

title: feat: enable native tool search through deployed SD Responses
body:
## Summary

Native tool search now runs through the deployed SD service `/v1/responses` endpoint on `superdav-chat-fast`, `superdav-chat-pro`, and `superdav-chat-strong`. The existing site token and OAuth backend remain the authentication and billing path. Service PR [#109](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-service/pull/109) is merged and deployed.

- Preserve complete native output, including encrypted reasoning, discovery calls/results, namespaces, function calls, and refusals. Replay it across fresh PHP requests, confirmations, and browser handoffs with `store: false`, `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`, and no `previous_response_id`.
- Bind encrypted one-day replay snapshots to site/session/user and model/endpoint/tool/credential scope, capped at 1 MiB. Ordinary SDK history remains authoritative; invalid or evicted snapshots use compatible full-history transport.
- Give native models direct-function routing instructions in `SystemInstructionBuilder`, and avoid duplicating the deferred catalog in the prose manifest. Keep the existing filter as an opt-out.
- If the automatic full catalog exceeds the local payload budget, retry with Tier 1 plus browser functions, retaining compatibility discovery for the remaining PHP abilities. Preflight happens before cursor lookup so this retry preserves native replay. Explicit ability lists and transport safety limits remain enforced.
- Keep refusals visible and preserve attachments through the compatible adapter; the deployed native route accepts text/tool history only.

Implementation and measured evidence: `docs/NATIVE_TOOL_SEARCH_CONTINUITY.md`. Regression tests cover encrypted replay, scope invalidation, native routing, managed model selection, refusal replay, bounded catalog recovery, attachment preservation, and SDK retries. The obsolete image test Reflection call was removed because PHP 8.5 rejects its deprecation in the isolated process; its assertions remain intact.

## Production validation — 2026-10-01

- All three managed aliases returned HTTP 200 with native `tool_search_call`, `tool_search_output`, and the requested deferred function call.
- A real AgentLoop read synthetic category calibration 7341, post duration 19 minutes, and answered 38 minutes across three user turns. All six requests stayed on Responses. Each follow-up replayed the exact prior native input plus output, including encrypted reasoning. Later turns used fresh PHP processes.
- A separate confirmation pause resumed successfully on Responses in a fresh PHP process.
- The real browser UI used the General agent's 203-function catalog. Bounded recovery produced a 65,091-byte request containing 33 functions. Native search found `sd-ai-agent-js/navigate-to`, its actual browser callback navigated to `plugins.php`, and the automatic resume returned HTTP 200 on Responses with exact native replay. The final reply remained visible after reloading the conversation. No Chat Completions fallback occurred in that browser run.
- Tests used separate disposable WordPress databases and synthetic content. Copied credentials were removed afterward; raw replay traces and tokens are excluded from the commit.

## Worker self-verification

- PHPUnit: Tests: 4506, Assertions: 21035, Errors: 0, Failures: 0, Skipped: 145, Incomplete: 4
- Lint:    PHP/JS/CSS all clean
- PHPStan: 0 errors
- Build:   succeeded
- Bundle:  budgets passed

`WP_PHPUNIT_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/sd-client-2701-phpunit WP_LIVE_DB_NAME=wordpress pnpm run verify` completed successfully using the PR's frozen lockfile dependencies. The isolated test database was `sd_ai_agent_native_2701_tests`. The build retained two webpack size warnings; all enforced bundle budgets passed.

## Limits

Native search does not make deferred schemas disappear from the HTTP envelope. Large catalogs use bounded native discovery plus the existing compatibility tools. Attachments and missing native snapshots use compatible transport. Local encrypted replay retention lasts up to one day. No speedup is claimed: the earlier three-tool comparison was not faster, and repeated representative performance benchmarking remains follow-up work.

title: fix: compact managed chat context before overflow
body:
## Problem

A short managed-chat request can fail with HTTP 400 `max_tokens_exceeded` after large read-only tool responses. The managed gateway conservatively counts serialized message bytes as input tokens, but the plugin's generic local request limit is 512 KiB. A captured failure sent about 280 KiB after an ability search and product listing; the gateway rejected it against the selected model's 200,000-token context limit.

## Change

- Bound managed chat requests by the model context window minus the advertised output limit, retaining the existing envelope safety margin. Other providers retain their configured limits.
- When even the current turn's tool results exceed that envelope, compact a provider-only copy **before** the model call. Restore the complete durable conversation afterward; do not replay tools or mutate the site as part of compaction.
- Keep a bounded receipt of WooCommerce product IDs, names, SKUs, and statuses so a follow-up action can select a product without resending entire REST records. Omit descriptions and metadata. Preserve bounded search arguments for inspection calls.

This uses the existing deterministic compaction machinery. OpenCode similarly budgets recent context and prunes oversized tool output before summarizing earlier history ([source](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts)); Codex retains user intent while replacing older history with a bounded summary ([source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/compact.rs)). The plugin avoids an extra paid summary request by keeping its current deterministic path and leaving the durable transcript unchanged.

## Worker self-verification

- PHPUnit: Tests: 4467, Assertions: 20899, Errors: 0, Failures: 0, Skipped: 141, Incomplete: 4 (`pnpm run test:php -- --no-coverage`, after rebasing onto current `main`)

- Focused regression: 3 tests, 17 assertions; synthetic discovery/product responses compact below 64 KiB while preserving coupon intent and product identity, with the full saved history intact.

title: fix: recover tool approval jobs after ambiguous responses
body:
## Summary

Fix chat job tracking after an approval or denial response fails, including the reported “Job not found or not awaiting confirmation” error while already-approved work continues.

- Share decision submission and recovery in `src/store/slices/jobSlice.js`, with the existing `confirmToolCall` and `rejectToolCall` entry points retained in `src/store/slices/sessionsSlice.js`.
- Submit each decision exactly once. On a failed response, resume the existing read-only job poller rather than retrying approval, inferring completion, or approving another tool batch.
- Update a processing job's session status even when no new tool activity has arrived, so “Approval needed” cannot remain stuck until the next tool result.
- Restore fresh pending tools or saved completed results through the existing polling paths. Stop promptly and display the server error when status reads are rejected; keep bounded retries for transient connection failures.
- Keep terminal UI cleanup scoped to the active session, protect a newer job from an old failed decision response, and centralize persisted-job cleanup when polling stops.

## Reproduction and regression coverage

The controlled REST reproduction at `edc46c28` showed that the first confirmation queues processing, while a second confirmation returns the exact reported 404 without cancelling that queued work. This PR fixes the frontend's handling of that ambiguous response; it does not claim that the original FluentCRM incident's precise trigger or execution without approval has been established.

- `tests/SdAiAgent/REST/ToolApprovalLifecycleTest.php`: first/duplicate confirmation, paused state without approval, and expired approval recovery, without provider calls or real CRM mutations.

title: fix: preserve native tool continuations and reduce discovery context
body:
Browser and confirmation continuations could fall from `/v1/responses` to Chat Completions because persisted tool results no longer matched the native history prefix. Unchanged JSON was re-encoded by the preview-URL redactor, and associative database decoding converted nested empty schema objects into arrays. Preserve unchanged JSON text, persist native tool results as JSON strings, and send those strings without encoding them again. Actual privacy redaction remains active.

Native search also loaded dozens of compatibility Tier-1 schemas immediately and restored the large capability manifest on bounded retries. Keep only small coordination tools immediate, group provider namespaces by domain, and retain compact bridge instructions and fetched schemas for partial catalogs. Existing ability identifiers and permission gates remain unchanged.

Separate the configured native HTTP body cap from the managed Chat byte-as-token context clamp. Include a development-only wp-env loopback helper so cron/background browser continuations reach Apache's internal container port, plus durable validation and benchmark guidance.

## Deployment dependency

**Dependency satisfied:** service PR #113 is merged and deployed. The final client revision was verified against the production service using the full catalog and normal output limit; see the post-deployment validation below.

Service dependency: https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-service/pull/113

Unrestricted full-catalog discovery, follow-up, confirmation, and browser navigation have now been repeated successfully. Existing connector credentials work; no customer toggle is needed.

## Post-deployment installed-site validation — 2026-10-02

Validated client revision `0ea3ceeb16b2acce712ba9a0941fb31d0b00d282` on the installed local WordPress site against the production service after #113 deployed. Used `superdav-chat-pro`, the full **203-function catalog (198 deferred)**, and the normal **16,384-token output limit**, with no temporary catalog cap or provider override.

Current PR revision `264e926113f23b8f2896d006ddd5335c32b4d9e9` adds only string-header normalization in the development loopback helper; production native-search code is unchanged from the tested revision. Verified the follow-up with PHPCS and live array/string-header loopback requests (both HTTP 200). Current PR CI checks are green, including PHPUnit, three Playwright shards, lint, static analysis, build and bundle checks.

- Three repeated long-tail discovery / draft-post retrieval / arithmetic follow-up conversations and three plugin-inventory inspections returned the expected answers. These runs used automatic tool selection rather than explicitly exposing a small tool list.
- Confirmation paused and resumed with approval in a fresh PHP process, retaining the full catalog and exact native replay.
- Three independent browser handoffs reached Plugins, Themes and Dashboard, with their persisted final replies verified. One exercised `ability-search` followed by browser navigation; the other two used ordinary navigation wording.
- A UI follow-up after navigation correctly identified the Plugins page and remained native.
- **32 full-catalog provider calls succeeded with HTTP 200, all `/v1/responses`; 22 continuation prefixes replayed exactly.** Zero Chat fallbacks, mismatched prefixes or `max_tokens_exceeded` errors. Requests ranged from 193,045 to 217,555 bytes; actual input ranged from 5,530 to 8,494 tokens per successful request.
- One separate browser attempt returned `wallet_balance_insufficient` (402) while CLI inference was also running. The same prompt passed after the CLI run finished, followed by two more successful isolated browser tests. This rejected request is retained and excluded from the pass count. It is consistent with concurrent conservative reservations, but account-ledger evidence was not collected to prove the cause. Credit admission remains a separate constraint; these changes do not establish billing or concurrency gains.

All 14 CLI validation steps passed, including confirmation pause/approval, plus the browser scenarios above. Temporary fixtures, owned test sessions and metadata-only diagnostics were cleaned up. No production code changed during this verification.

Native-only full-catalog medians: content conversation **36,526 input tokens / 30.51s**, plugin inventory **13,960 input tokens / 11.27s**. These use different discovery scope from the earlier paired bounded-catalog benchmarks and do not establish a new speed or billing comparison.

## All-model regression and wallet investigation — 2026-10-02

Tested all three managed chat models against the deployed service using existing connector credentials, on client revision `264e926113f23b8f2896d006ddd5335c32b4d9e9`.

| Model | Plain text | Full-catalog tool task | Installed chat UI |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fast / Speedy | Pass | Pass | Pass |
| Pro | Pass | Pass | Previously verified |
| Strong | Pass | Pass | Not repeated |

The six CLI cases and Fast UI inventory task produced **11 HTTP 200 calls, all `/v1/responses`**. Tool cases used 203 functions, 198 deferred, with normal model output limits (Fast 8,192; Pro/Strong 16,384). No catalog cap or customer toggle.

Verified isolated `main` class overrides reproduce the reported Fast failure: the full request is 196,899 bytes and its bounded retry is 102,957 bytes, both exceeding the old 87,040-byte local budget. It fails with `sd_ai_agent_provider_payload_budget_exceeded` before inference. Pro and Strong pass on old main only after a bounded retry. The native HTTP body budget fix already in this PR resolves Fast's reproduced failure.

The earlier 402 came from the local site's **unlinked promotional wallet**, not the maintainer's account showing $8.59. Its cached balance was $10 while a live refresh returned $2.188399 before this investigation. During subsequent verification a cached available balance of $0.709994 returned to $1.518674 after settlement. The exact ledger for the earlier rejected request and the reported $8.59 account have not been inspected.

Service reservations still conservatively count serialized native request bytes, including deferred schemas, and reserve the requested maximum output. The deployed context fix excludes those deferred schemas from context admission, but it does not reduce wallet reservations. At the repository's default Pro rate, a 193,045-byte body with 16,384 maximum output implies a hold of **at least $1.456745** before JSON wrapping/escaping, despite much smaller actual usage. This is a source-derived lower bound, not a measurement of the live rate card or the rejected request's reservation. Do not attribute an $8.59 balance rejection to this test wallet without checking account identity and outstanding reservations.

For the same inventory task, current Pro/Strong used 12,964 / 13,992 total input tokens versus 39,126 / 39,127 on verified old main. These single comparisons support context reduction, not a speed or billing claim. Invalid class-override setup runs were excluded from baseline results. Tracked CLI test sessions and temporary diagnostics were removed; the browser test chat was preserved after automatic cleanup review rejected its deletion. Metadata-only results remain local.

## Pre-deployment bounded-catalog validation

- Three repaired browser navigation sessions stayed on `/v1/responses`, with HTTP 200 and exact native input/output-prefix replay. Each reached `plugins.php`.
- A UI follow-up after navigation correctly identified the Plugins page and remained native.
- A confirmation paused and resumed with approval in a fresh PHP process; both provider calls remained native with exact replay.
- Browser validation deliberately used a bounded 30-function catalog while the deployed service still has its old admission check. This validates the replay fix, not full-catalog production deployment.
- Earlier unrestricted long-tail lookup attempts with a partial catalog gave incomplete answers or exhausted retries. Full-catalog and follow-up probes hit the deployed context guard. These remain rollout limitations, rather than successful production tests.

## Pre-deployment bounded-catalog benchmarks

Three counterbalanced paired trials used the same model, user, credentials, fixtures and permissions. All twelve complete workloads returned the expected answers. Content includes three user turns with taxonomy lookup, post retrieval and follow-up arithmetic; inventory inspects installed/active plugins. Usage totals include every provider request. Content exposes the same three functions to both modes; inventory uses the same bounded 45-function catalog. These comparisons include prompt-manifest and deferral improvements.

| Whole-task median | Native input | Compatibility input | Reduction | Native time | Compatibility time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Content conversation | 31,055 | 80,400 | 61.4% | 23.24s | 20.47s |
| Plugin inventory | 11,351 | 38,394 | 70.4% | 8.35s | 9.39s |

A separate matched-prompt first-call control supplied the same 46 functions without the large capability manifest: native deferred 42 functions and used a median **1,497 input tokens**, versus **8,350** for eager Chat Completions (**82.1% less**). This compares Responses with Chat, rather than isolating deferral within one protocol, and is not a complete task. Eager Responses controls were rejected upstream and fell back to Chat; they are excluded from that successful control comparison.

These measurements establish context reduction, not general speed or billing gains. Compatibility was heavily cached: median uncached input was 3,600 versus native 19,316 for content, and 506 versus native 6,487 for inventory. Timings measure synchronous AgentLoop execution, not browser queue wait. Recheck cache behavior and complete-task performance after service deployment.

title: GH#2721 GH#2722 GH#2723: Simple safe MCP connections and OAuth sign-in
body:
Resolves #2721
Resolves #2722
Resolves #2723

## Summary

One combined implementation for the simple MCP connection manager, modern HTTP safety boundary, and OAuth sign-in. Keep this PR **draft and unmerged for maintainer testing**; no release is requested.

- `src/settings-page/mcp-integrations-manager.js` adds URL-first setup, optional names, static authentication, OAuth redirects, Advanced registered-client details, connection status, discovered tools, refresh/edit/remove, and credential-free import/export.
- `includes/Mcp/RemoteMcpOAuthClient.php`, `RemoteMcpOAuthStateRepository.php`, and `includes/Bootstrap/RemoteMcpOAuthHandler.php` provide authorization-code/S256 PKCE, validated metadata/resource/issuer binding, one-time current-user/site-bound state, encrypted token storage, refresh/rotation, and disconnect. Callback returns to the actual `#/settings` route and Tools tab.
- `includes/Mcp/RemoteMcpClient.php`, `RemoteMcpHttpTransport.php`, `RemoteMcpPolicy.php`, and `RemoteMcpLock.php` bound discovery/execution and validate protocol, response IDs, arguments and results. Generation/revision/lease fences protect credential and snapshot commits; ambiguous tool calls are not replayed.
- `includes/Abilities/OptionsAbilities.php` blocks MCP credentials and OAuth state from generic option reads/writes, and blocks generic registry writes. MCP traffic is excluded from provider traces/cache rewriting.
- Remote hints do not bypass local confirmation policy. Returned tool data is explicitly untrusted; local WordPress ability IDs accept underscore/Unicode remote names while preserving the exact remote tool name and collision-resistant suffix.
- `includes/Mcp/RemoteMcpAbilityRegistrar.php` generates compact connection/tool-bound IDs so complete SDK function names fit the 64-character provider limit. `includes/Infrastructure/AiClient/Superdav/SuperdavAiResponsesToolSearchTextGenerationModel.php` keeps ability-search and ability-call immediately available; operational tools remain deferred. Regression coverage verifies bounded names, distinct connections, and non-deferred compatibility dispatch.
- `includes/REST/McpConnectionsController.php` validates advanced OAuth details and all imported endpoints before writing connections. Regression tests cover invalid credentials and an unsafe later import entry.
- `DESIGN.md`, `README.md`, and `docs/outbound-mcp.md` document the simplified flow and compatibility limits. Mobile actions stack and meet a 44px minimum touch target.

## Scope and compatibility

- Modern Streamable HTTP only; no legacy HTTP+SSE transport, stdio/command execution, persistent listener, background scheduler, custom schema engine, or general OAuth platform.
- Protocol negotiation supports 2026-07-28, 2025-11-25 and 2025-06-18.
- OAuth supports Client ID Metadata Documents where advertised, or Advanced pre-registered client details. Dynamic client registration is deliberately unsupported and explained to the user.
- Maintains the canonical `sd-ai-agent/` internal namespaces and `superdav-ai-agent` text domain.

## Runtime acceptance evidence

Installed the built branch on the existing development site and exercised the real Settings → Tools manager with a **development-only mocked HTTP/OAuth fixture**, not an external provider:

- Ordinary browser clicks open Add server and submit setup after scrolling controls into view.
- No-auth connection discovers one tool and reports Connected.
- OAuth PKCE redirect/callback returns to Tools and reports Connected; disconnect disables execution; Sign in again restores the connection.
- Both discovered `demo_greet` tools execute through registered WordPress abilities and return a greeting inside the untrusted-output wrapper.
- After maintainer reported the actual chat failure, reproduced the gap beyond direct execution: the old generated function names were 77 characters, and the search/call bridge was deferred. Verified a fresh Standard-model chat after both repairs: ability-search found the demo; the normal confirmation appeared; after one-time Allow, ability-call successfully executed `demo_greet` with `name: Dave`, and the UI listed the remote tool as Completed and returned “Hello Dave from the local MCP demo.” No always-allow setting was changed. `docs/outbound-mcp.md` now requires chat-level acceptance, not only Connected status/direct execution.
- Anonymous manager REST requests return HTTP 401 `rest_forbidden`.
- Desktop 1280×900 and mobile 390×844 viewport screenshots received an independent, read-only layout review: no observed clipping, overlap, unreadable controls, or horizontal overflow in the shown area. Mobile Add server measured 44px high; page width 375px in a 390px viewport.

The fixture and local TLS/authentication support are not shipped or committed. External interoperability and real provider consent remain maintainer acceptance work; this evidence does not claim those were tested. After installing a new build, hard-refresh the page to replace cached route stylesheets.

## Reopened and merged with main (2026-10-13)

The pulse closed this PR for merge conflicts. It was reopened, `origin/main` (23 commits) was merged in, and the result was re-reviewed:

- Only conflict: `scripts/check-bundle-size.js` deferred-JS cap (main raised it to 1724/529 KiB; this PR to 1732/532). Rebuilt and set the cap to the measured combined size.
- Main's GH#2813 text-domain fix: all new MCP UI/PHP strings already use `superdav-ai-agent`; `sd-ai-agent` occurrences are canonical internal IDs only.
- All six CodeRabbit threads were checked against the code and are fixed: atomic `INSERT IGNORE` lease with cache invalidation, AES-256-GCM static secrets, `client_secret` removed from OAuth state, revoke falls back from empty refresh token, and list-valued schema types/`pattern` are supported.
- Fix (`includes/Mcp/RemoteMcpPolicy.php`): PHPStan on the merged tree flagged `array_diff()` on an untrusted `type` list. A hostile schema like `"type": [["x"]]` would trigger an Array-to-string conversion. Every type member must now be a supported string.
- Cleanup (`includes/Mcp/RemoteMcpConnectionRepository.php`): removed a dead duplicate `configured` assignment in `public_connection()`. It was overwritten right away and caused an extra secrets read.

## Worker self-verification
- PHPUnit: Tests: 4587, Assertions: 21494, Errors: 0, Failures: 0, Skipped: 145, Incomplete: 4
- Lint:    PHP/JS/CSS all clean
- PHPStan: 0 errors
- Build:   succeeded
- Bundle:  budgets passed

Post-merge run: PHPUnit ran against the dedicated `wordpress_test` database with an isolated cache, not the live development database. MCP manager Jest suite: 4/4 passed.

Additional required option-security/MCP regression run: `pnpm run test:php -- --filter='OptionsAbilitiesTest|WordPressAbilitiesTest|DatabaseAbilitiesTest|WpCliAbilitiesTest|RemoteMcp'` — 109 tests, 669 assertions, zero errors/failures, one skipped. Manager Jest suite: four tests passed.

## Bundle budget decision

`scripts/check-bundle-size.js` records the measured aggregate deferred-JavaScript increase, measured after merging main: 1,736.9 KiB minified / 531.9 KiB gzip, with caps 1,738 / 533 KiB. Launch caps and largest deferred-asset caps are unchanged. Floating widget: 90.8 / 28.0 KiB; widget panel: 99.7 / 26.6 KiB; largest deferred asset: 262.4 / 84.5 KiB. Existing webpack asset-size advisories remain warnings, not failed checks.

## Maintainer testing

Open AI Agent → Settings → Tools → MCP servers. Check the installed no-auth and OAuth demo connections, expand View discovered tools/Details, try refresh, disable/re-enable, and disconnect/sign-in again. For real-server acceptance, add a public HTTPS modern HTTP endpoint, choose its authentication method, and use Advanced only when a registered client is required. Confirm the normal tool approval policy remains in effect before executing a remote tool.

For chat acceptance, start a new conversation and ask: “Use the Local MCP demo server's demo_greet tool to say hi to Dave.” Approve Allow when prompted; check the completed remote tool and returned greeting. Exact server/tool naming avoids interpreting “great tool” as a different server rather than `demo_greet`.

## Maintainer acceptance results (2026-10-13, merged head)

Run on the shared dev site with the canonical `superdav-ai-agent` plugin symlink pointing at this branch. The site was served through the local HTTPS dev proxy (`https://wordpress.local:8443`), using the existing dev-only mocked fixture mu-plugin (not shipped). Driven by Playwright with real clicks.

Settings → Tools → MCP servers (20/20 passed):
- Both demo connections Connected; View discovered tools lists `demo_greet`; Details show no secret values.
- Refresh tools shows "Tools refreshed."; Disable → Disabled; re-enable → Connected (fresh discovery).
- OAuth: Disconnect sign-in → "Authentication required"; Sign in again → PKCE redirect/callback → `mcp_oauth=connected`, lands on Tools tab, Connected.
- Export lists both servers and contains no credentials.
- Mobile 390×844: Add server is 44px; no horizontal overflow. Anonymous `GET /wp-json/sd-ai-agent/v1/mcp-connections` → HTTP 401. No page JS errors from plugin code.
- Found and fixed during acceptance: the section showed "MCP servers" twice (settings section title plus the component's own `<h3>`). Commit `0bbcc85a` removes the inner heading.

Chat (Standard model, new conversation):
- Prompt: "Use the Local MCP demo server's demo_greet tool to say hi to Dave."
- The normal Tool Confirmation dialog appeared ("Always allow" unchecked). One-time Allow → reply "Hello Dave from the local MCP demo."
- Plugin option fingerprints before/after: only `sd_ai_agent_ability_usage` changed; no permission/always-allow settings changed.

Observations (non-blocking, follow-up candidates):
- The confirmation dialog shows the generated function name (`wpab__sd-ai-agent__mcp-demo-greet-<hash>`) rather than a friendly "demo_greet on Local MCP demo" label.
- OAuth sign-in on a plain-HTTP site returns HTTP 500 `sd_ai_agent_remote_mcp_oauth_https_required`. The message is correct, but a 4xx status would be more accurate.

CI on `0bbcc85a`: Build & Bundle Size, Lint, PHPUnit, Static Analysis, Playwright E2E shards 1–3, canonical identifiers, CodeRabbit — all pass.

title: GH#2698: preserve originating chats during multisite navigation
body:
## Summary

Resolves #2698.

- Resolve admin-relative filenames with `get_admin_url( $blog_id, $path )`, including subdirectory, subdomain, and local-port multisite installations.
- Return validated cross-blog destinations as user-operated links instead of moving the originating chat. Keep current-user capability checks and same-site navigation's result-before-unload ordering.
- Reject duplicated admin prefixes, unknown-blog admin paths, traversal/ambiguous URL encodings, credentials, iframe links, and external hosts.
- Keep the PHP/browser navigation catalogs and multisite context guidance aligned. Clear stale deferred targets on refused navigation or link responses.

## URL writer and scope

The old expression in `src/abilities/navigation.js`, `'/wp-admin/' + path.replace( /^\//, '' )`, reproduces `/wp-admin/woo/wp-admin/plugins.php` when given `woo/wp-admin/plugins.php`. It also incorrectly targets the network root when called with `plugins.php` from a subsite. The replacement asks WordPress to resolve and validate the destination; it never repairs arbitrary path segments by guessing.

The original compact transcript does not prove that this callback ran during the reported incident. The owning external integration was inspected read-only: `Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite` registers `multisite-ultimate/site-create-item` through `inc/apis/trait-mcp-abilities.php`; `mcp_create_item()` returns `item => $item->to_array()`, and `inc/models/class-site.php::to_array()` includes the created site's ID. That path does not emit an admin redirect. No external integration repair is claimed, and no WooCommerce installation/activation was performed.

Two additional implementation files were necessary beyond the brief's candidate list: `includes/Core/ClientAbilityRouter.php` is the actual server-to-browser navigation handoff and must not turn `action: link` back into automatic navigation; `includes/Abilities/Js/JsAbilityCatalog.php` owns the canonical browser descriptor and must advertise the same inputs/output. No session-sharing subsystem, impersonation, or capability bypass was added.

- Existing job polling code still submits the browser result before consuming the deferred same-site navigation; focused job/approval tests passed.

Direct final diff inspection plus independent advisory security/correctness review found no remaining blocker. The exact rebased review bundle is SHA-256 `3b3c47d6e4966c5406ee1f1f38e97acac28dfabf49bdeb62b0d6f5b2e0b62d5c` (prompt-injection scan clean).

title: GH#2842: compact completed-turn tool payloads in provider requests
body:
## Summary

This addresses the main remaining cause of context bloat after #2832, #2833, #2835, #2836 and #2839: **tool results and arguments from completed turns were replayed verbatim on every later provider request.**

- `includes/Core/CompletedTurnCompactor.php` (new): compacts tool payloads from completed turns in the provider view only. Results over 2 KB are replaced by a 1 KB UTF-8-safe excerpt and a recovery note ("call the tool again…"). Large arguments keep short top-level scalars such as IDs and slugs and stay valid JSON. Running it again on its own output changes nothing. Durable session history, checkpoints and the UI transcript are unchanged.
- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php`: `run()` records its own user message as the turn boundary, so mid-turn guidance messages cannot move it. Chat Completions history before that message is compacted. Resumed runs have no known boundary and skip compaction.
- `SuperdavAiResponsesToolSearchTextGenerationModel.php`: native replay compacts items by completed-turn `call_id`, so the SDK prefix hash that matches the stored cursor is unchanged. The stored snapshot holds the compacted form. The Chat Completions fallback is compacted too.
- `ResponsesContinuation::prune_completed_discovery()`: completed turns keep one copy of each called schema, at its earliest load.

## Evidence (fake-provider replay, real abilities and session persistence)

The harness runs this worktree's plugin in the shared dev site, intercepts `/responses` and `/chat/completions` at `pre_http_request`, and replays a 10-turn onboarding chat with read-only tool calls.

| Turn 10 | Before (main 774fb3de) | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Native model-visible bytes | 187,843 (over the 183,616 gateway limit) | 81,133 |
| Native `function_call_output` | 116,533 | 20,949 |
| Native completed `tool_search_output` | 30,145 | 19,037 |
| Chat Completions request | 165,952, locally rejected, then reduced retry on every request from turn 7 | 70,208, no rejections |

Single largest replayed item: `get-global-styles` at 30,171 bytes.

Ruled out as the main cause: system instructions are 13–27 KB and stable per turn, Tier 1 schemas are about 14 KB, and completed reasoning is already pruned by #2835.

## Rebase onto #2844 and #2845

Conflict in `generateTextResult()` resolved so compaction applies to both cursor replay and #2844's local-history replay after cursor loss. Re-measured peak model-visible bytes over all 10 turns: native 83,786; Chat Completions 65,280; native with cursor dropped at turn 8: 83,626 (stays on `/responses`, 0 local rejections).

## Follow-ups (now merged)

- #2840 Current-turn results are still unbounded: `ToolResultTruncator` does not reduce deep associative maps (`get-global-styles` stays at 30,171 bytes after truncation). This drives the remaining within-turn peak of about 120 KB on theme turns.
- #2841 A lost native replay cursor makes every later turn build a rejected 270 KB full-catalog Chat Completions request before the Tier 1 retry.

## Worker self-verification
- PHPUnit: Tests: 4607, Assertions: 21540, Errors: 0, Failures: 0, Skipped: 145, Incomplete: 4 (rebased on #2844 + #2845)
- Lint:    PHP/JS/CSS all clean
- PHPStan: 0 errors
- Build:   succeeded
- Bundle:  budgets passed

Focused: `CompletedTurnCompactorTest|ResponsesContinuationTest` → OK (25 tests, 107 assertions).

Not verified: a live managed-gateway request. The fake-provider harness checks request shape and size only, not that the provider accepts the compacted excerpts.

Resolves #2842
